_comment: Canonical template_answer shapes per category, extracted from the manually verified RepoBehave benchmark (qa_instances/, 1333 oracles). Generation agents MUST use one of these templates verbatim (exact keys, exact nesting); they must never invent new keys or rename existing ones. 'varies' notes the only allowed deviations. Global key conventions: 'file' = repo-relative path (e.g. 'haystack/core/pipeline/base.py'); 'func' = dotted module.qualname (e.g. 'haystack.core.pipeline.base.PipelineBase.connect'); tests are referenced by pytest id strings.

templates.use_for: the exact ordered sequence of executed line events inside the target for a stated invocation
templates.varies: nothing — keys, nesting, and types are fixed

templates.use_for: iteration count of one specific loop (identified by header line) for a stated invocation
the value of a named loop variable at a specific iteration
templates.varies: the type of 'value' may be 'int', 'float', or 'str' to match the actual data

templates.use_for: values of named locals at a precise observation point
templates.varies: nothing structural; values are repr strings

templates.use_for: ordered history of one variable's values during an invocation
templates.varies: nothing structural; values are repr strings

templates.use_for: flat ordered list of repr values a variable takes

S3_ProgramState.notes: State questions legitimately vary more than other categories, but prefer these shapes; if none fits, reuse their key style (snake_case, 'variable'/'value' vocabulary, repr-string values) rather than inventing new vocabulary.

templates.use_for: all def-use questions — 114 of 118 verified S4 instances use exactly this shape
templates.varies: nothing — keys, nesting, and types are fixed; never use 'var', 'file', or per-invocation maps

templates.use_for: the single exception raised/propagated in the scenario (type + exact str(exc))
the set of exception types caught during the run (state sort order in the question)
how many times a named function is invoked during the test
maximum call depth within a named call chain (define depth counting in the question)
the ordered sequence of tracked function calls (state the tracked set and inclusion rule in the question)
cross-function executed line path
the sorted set of the target's lines executed at least once during the whole test — the dominant verified M1 shape
max/min iteration counts of a loop across invocations
total iterations of a loop across the whole test
which test cases exit the loop via break (pytest id strings, sorted)
extrema of a traced numeric variable across the run
templates.varies: types may be 'int' when the variable is integral

templates.use_for: extrema plus the variable name when the question tracks one of several
templates.varies: types may be 'int' when the variable is integral

templates.use_for: the sorted set of distinct repr values a variable takes

M3_ProgramState.notes: Like S3, some structural variation is tolerated, but reuse this vocabulary instead of inventing keys.

templates.use_for: all M4 def-use questions — identical shape to S4; hardness comes from the scenario, not the schema
which test cases crash (with what exception type) vs complete safely
the exception types observed during the run (state sort order in the question)
the set of tracked functions executed at least once (state sort order) — the dominant verified M6 shape
which concrete implementations a dynamic dispatch site selected, in order
whether a single stated predicate held at every observation — the dominant verified M7 shape (the predicate goes in the QUESTION, verbatim)
one predicate checked across loop iterations with violation accounting
whether a variable was strictly_increasing / non_decreasing / constant / none across iterations (enumerate the allowed strings in the question)
